extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors/writers querying literary agents (people preparing query letters and submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on common reasons a literary agent will reject a query and concrete advice for avoiding those pitfalls when writing query letters (especially for novels and memoirs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir: no overarching theme.
rubrics_metrics.description: The memoir was largely 'this terrible but interesting thing happened to us' but there was no sense of how that would resonate with readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: if you're writing memoir, you MUST answer the question 'why would anyone else care about this.' Your story must have utility for me. I'll read about sad stories on the internet but I'm not going to pay $25 for a hardcover book if the only thing it's about is your struggle with cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the novel is so abstract as to be meaningless.
rubrics_metrics.description: The query is too abstract—often lacking character names—making the description meaningless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: Read QueryShark. Or any other query critique site. Apply what you learn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of a novel I don't want to read.
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent simply doesn't want to read the kind of book described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: you can't. Sometimes you're just going to query someone who doesn't want to read your book. Suck it up and move on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the plot made no sense to me
rubrics_metrics.description: (and because I was doing this list I was NOT skimming) — the plot description in the query is incoherent or unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: ask someone to answer the Who What Why questions about your novel based solely on the query. If they can't do it, it's time to revise.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-dimensional characters; plot so far-fetched I laughed.
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters lack depth and the plot sounds unbelievable or ridiculous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: write better. This is text book bad writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: A juvenile book that seriously misunderstands what kids like to read
rubrics_metrics.description: A children's/juvenile manuscript that doesn't reflect an understanding of the children's market or what kids actually enjoy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: know the market. If you're writing books for kids, it will help if you've read a lot of them. Also, anything that smacks of 'should' is generally a non-starter with kids.

rubrics_metrics.name: All set up (rife with stereotypes) and no plot
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission is mostly set-up and stereotyping without a driving plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: get plot on the page. There's a formula for that at QueryShark. Go find it. Use it.

rubrics_metrics.name: All character described in sexual terms.
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters are presented primarily in sexualized terms, which is boring and one-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: don't do it. If you don't see this problem, you need better beta readers. Yes, beta readers for your query is a good idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing is not publishable: confusing query, pages over-laden with adjectives.
rubrics_metrics.description: The prose/signals in the query and sample pages suggest the writing itself isn't at a publishable level (confusing prose, adjective overload).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: write better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading with themes that I am not much interested in; plot description can't save this
rubrics_metrics.description: The query foregrounds themes the agent doesn't care for, and the subsequent plot description doesn't overcome that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: you can't. Sometimes you just have a book I don't want to read. Query onward.

rubrics_metrics.name: No plot of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission lacks any sense of plot or direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #2 (make sure your query clearly conveys the plot and who the characters are).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unenticing, but decent writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The prose may be competent, but the premise or presentation fails to entice the agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #10 (work on making premise/lead more compelling; some agents simply won't be interested in certain themes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uninteresting premise
rubrics_metrics.description: The core idea or premise of the book fails to interest the agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #10 (sometimes you cannot change an agent's taste; query other agents).

rubrics_metrics.name: No plot.
rubrics_metrics.description: Again: the submission contains events but no organizing plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #2 (clarify the plot in your query).

rubrics_metrics.name: I don't understand the premise of the novel.
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent cannot grasp the book's premise from the query.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #4 (have someone else answer Who/What/Why based only on the query; revise until they can).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overwrought descriptions leading to suspect prose.
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive, overwrought description in the query led the agent to expect similar overwrought prose in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: Write better; tone down overwrought description so voice and clarity shine through.

rubrics_metrics.name: No plot — events but no plot.
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission reads as a series of events without narrative drive or stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #2 (structure the query to show the protagonist's goal and obstacles; convey stakes).

rubrics_metrics.name: The question of who would want to read this book is 'no one I know'
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent cannot identify an audience who would buy or care about the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: You can't. Query others who might recognize the audience; different agents have different lists/tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: The premise of the novel is just wildly clueless.
rubrics_metrics.description: The core premise demonstrates a failure of craft or understanding; it reads as implausible or naive in a way that can't be salvaged by voice alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: Read more. Watch how other writers successfully introduce things that may not be realistic but feel authentic in the book. It's harder than it looks.

rubrics_metrics.name: A query that is a textbook illustration of what NOT to do (including failing to answer 'what is the story about')
rubrics_metrics.description: The query exemplifies common query mistakes and fails to state what the story is about clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: Read QueryShark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does not understand what 'a novel' means.
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission suggests the writer doesn't grasp the form/requirements of a novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: I don't have a single clue here other than taking your query to a writers conference and asking an agent what's wrong with it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category is one I do not represent.
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript falls into a genre/category the agent does not represent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: Don't (i.e., don't expect representation from this agent for that category). Better to query me and hear no than miss out on me saying yes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Write what you know' taken too literally / thinly disguised author-as-protagonist
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Write what you know' assumptions can lead to bland, mundane material or unrealistic portrayals (e.g., thinly disguised authors-as-protagonists that are hampered by reality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: Thinly disguised authors-as-protagonists are often hampered by reality. 'A real doctor would never behave like House.' That is indeed true but this is a story, not reality TV. The whole reason for novels is to transcend and illuminate reality, not endlessly repeat it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir with no effort to answer why anyone would want to read this (repeat of #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A memoir that fails to demonstrate broader relevance or stakes—no effort to answer the larger question of why anyone would care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: See #1 (make clear why readers will care; show utility or larger relevance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Query letter is entirely about my submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.description: The query focuses on the agent's submission guidelines rather than describing the novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you will avoid this: tell me about the novel. (I've read my submission guidelines. More than once.)
